Guide

Hotel Lobby AI template: the complete guide

What is the Hotel Lobby AI template?

The Hotel Lobby AI template is the viral video format you have seen all over TikTok, Reels and Shorts: two performers trading verses in the iconic orange-booth stage, with the hanging mic, warm spotlight and moody backdrop. Until recently, making one meant filming in a real venue or stitching together edits. ViralReel turns it into a one-minute job — the template stages both performers automatically from two uploaded photos, syncs their lips and gestures to the beat, and renders a vertical 9:16 video that is ready to post.

Why the Hotel Lobby AI template went viral

Three reasons. First, the format is instantly recognizable — the orange booth is a visual hook, so viewers stop scrolling. Second, it is a two-person format, which means every video doubles your audience: both performers share it, and pet owners, couples and friends all want their own version. Third, the barrier to entry collapsed. What used to require a camera crew now needs two photos and about sixty seconds, so thousands of creators can join the trend the same week it peaks. That mix of recognition and accessibility is exactly why the format keeps spawning variants — couples, best friends, dogs and cats, parents and babies.

How to get the best results from the Hotel Lobby AI template

Photo quality decides video quality. Use one clear, front-facing photo per performer — good lighting, no sunglasses or heavy motion blur, and the full face in frame. Keep each performer on the same side across your photos so the AI keeps identities stable, and avoid group photos where faces overlap. Pick the variant that matches your subjects: the classic version for two people, the pet edition for dogs and cats, the pet-owner edition for you and your animal, or the baby version for family clips. Generate, preview, and post while the trend is still climbing — consistency beats perfection, and creators who publish three to five videos in a row see the strongest reach.

Frequently asked questions about ViralReel

How much does ViralReel cost?

Plus is $19.9/mo with 200 credits. Pro is $39.9/mo with 500 credits. Video costs vary by resolution and duration; failed or canceled jobs are refunded.

Why do I need two photos?

The format is a two-person back-and-forth performance. Two separate front-facing photos keep each identity clean and prevent face blending.

Can I use pets or babies?

Absolutely — pet and baby versions are the most-shared variants of the trend. Just keep each performer on their own side in every photo you upload.

What happens to my photos?

Photos are used only to render your video and are automatically deleted after 24 hours. We never train models on your uploads.

Do I own the videos I make?

Yes. Videos you generate are yours to post anywhere — TikTok, Reels, Shorts or client work. No watermark on paid plans, no strings attached.

What is the Hotel Lobby AI template?

The Hotel Lobby AI template is the viral video format you have seen all over TikTok, Reels and Shorts: two performers trading verses in the iconic orange-booth stage, with the hanging mic, warm spotlight and moody backdrop. Until recently, making one meant filming in a real venue or stitching together edits. ViralReel turns it into a one-minute job — the template stages both performers automatically from two uploaded photos, syncs their lips and gestures to the beat, and renders a vertical 9:16 video that is ready to post.

Why the Hotel Lobby AI template went viral

三个原因。 First, the format is instantly recognizable — the orange booth is a visual hook, so viewers stop scrolling. Second, it is a two-person format, which means every video doubles your audience: both performers share it, and pet owners, couples and friends all want their own version. Third, the barrier to entry collapsed. What used to require a camera crew now needs two photos and about sixty seconds, so thousands of creators can join the trend the same week it peaks. That mix of recognition and accessibility is exactly why the format keeps spawning variants — couples, best friends, dogs and cats, parents and babies.

How to get the best results from the Hotel Lobby AI template

Photo quality decides video quality. Use one clear, front-facing photo per performer — good lighting, no sunglasses or heavy motion blur, and the full face in frame. Keep each performer on the same side across your photos so the AI keeps identities stable, and avoid group photos where faces overlap. Pick the variant that matches your subjects: the classic version for two people, the pet edition for dogs and cats, the pet-owner edition for you and your animal, or the baby version for family clips. Generate, preview, and post while the trend is still climbing — consistency beats perfection, and creators who publish three to five videos in a row see the strongest reach.
